subject: SCIM delta + SSO assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ access-lineage
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@cleararc.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SCIM delta + SSO assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ access-lineage

Alyssa —

Quick note as we consolidate the SIG/CAIQ packet for your assessor: the review team asked for a compact "access lineage" deliverable that ties your identity source into roles and last-auth events. To close the loop we need two items from your side:

1) A SCIM delta export (CSV is fine) showing user-to-group changes for the past 90 days. Columns: timestamp, action (create/update/delete), user_id, primary_email, group_id, group_name, source (okta/azure/other).
2) A small sample of SAML assertions (anonymized) for two typical flows: a web login and a provisioning-triggered assertion. Redact any PII but preserve assertion attributes (NameID, attributes/roles, audience, issueInstant).

If we can get these by EOD Thu (4/4) the SOC reviewer should be satisfied for the access-control traceability section. I attached our suggested mapping workbook (access-lineage-mapping.xlsx) that shows how we'll consume the SCIM rows into our evidence table.

Let me know if the CSV layout above is painful and we can accept JSON or a short export instead.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: access-lineage-mapping.xlsx

From: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@cleararc.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cleararc.com, procurement@cleararc.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SSO assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ access-lineage

Ben —

Thanks, we can provide both. A few quick clarifications before we package:

- For SCIM deltas we have a weekly delta export from Okta; it includes event_type and actor fields in addition to the columns you listed. We can trim to your exact columns.
- For SAML assertion samples we need to anonymize NameIDs and IPs. We'll provide two redacted .txt files with the assertion XML and a one-line context note (e.g., "interactive web login, user agent Chrome 114").
- Our security team prefers we share assertions via a secured Drive folder (link will be shared) rather than inline email.

We aim to drop the SCIM CSV and two assertion samples into the Drive folder by Wed 4/3 EOD PST. Is that timing still ok for your reviewer?

Attached: scim-delta-sample.csv (first 100 rows, trimmed) — sensitive fields redacted.

Best,
Alyssa King
Director, Security & Compliance
ClearArc Health
alyssa.king@cleararc.com | (617) 555-9987

Attachments: scim-delta-sample.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@cleararc.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SSO assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ access-lineage

Alyssa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the sample CSV — timing is perfect. A couple of micro-asks to make ingestion smoother:

- Please keep the original event timestamp in ISO8601 (UTC) and add a column "source_event_id" if available.
- If actor is present, good to include it; we'll map to "changed_by" in the workbook.
- For assertions, please include the assertion's Audience and SubjectConfirmationMethod fields (even if redacted). Those are the specific checks the assessor looks for.

Naomi — can you take the SCIM sample and drop it into the mapping workbook, then flag any columns we need to ask ClearArc for before finalizing?

Laura — FYI — this is the ClearArc SIG packet that dovetails with the contract renewal later this quarter.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Alyssa King <alyssa.king@cleararc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Apr 2028 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SCIM delta + SSO assertion samples for SIG/CAIQ access-lineage

Alyssa / Ben —

I pulled the attached scim-delta-sample.csv into the workbook and ran a quick reconciliation. High-level notes:

- File looks good; we can map timestamp -> event_time, action -> event_type, user_id/email -> principal_id/principal_email, group_id/name -> resource_id/resource_name.
- Missing: source_event_id (ok if you can't provide), and we don't have a stable "role" attribute in the SCIM export — there are group names that imply roles (e.g., "app_admins") but no explicit role claim. If you have a derived attribute or admin flag in Okta, that would be helpful for the SOC traceability narrative.
- Sample SAML assertions (received in Drive) contain the Audience and NameID formats — thanks for redacting. I pasted two assertion snippets into the evidence sheet.

Next steps: I'll finalize the access-lineage tab and export an evidence bundle (CSV + narrative) for the SIG reviewer by Monday 4/8. If procurement needs a separate invoice or contract redline while we finish the SIG packet, please loop Proc.

Naomi Feldman
Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: access-lineage-mapping.xlsx, evidence-bundle-preview.csv
